newsitem.title: FINLAND: ERM PEG NOT POLITICAL DECISION ON EMU -LIPPONEN.
newsitem.headline: ERM PEG NOT POLITICAL DECISION ON EMU -LIPPONEN.

text.p: Finland's decision to link the markka to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) was not a political decision to join Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Thursday.
He repeated an earlier view that the peg makes sure Finland fulfils the criterion on currency stability so that the government will be able to have a true choice.
"A political decision to join the third stage of EMU among the first was not made through the ERM peg," he said in a prepared speech to parliament.
He said the importance of ERM memberhsip had repeatedly been stressed in talks between the European Monetary Insitute (EMI), the EU, the Finnish government and the Bank of Finland.
"Views on the necessity of an ERM-link has strengthened further lately," he said.
"Among others, German central bank governor Hans Tietmeyer and EMI President Alexandre Lamfallussy have clearly brought out their views that ERM-membership is required," he added.
Parliament was debating the issue after Lipponen's speech, but no vote or decision was scheduled.
